shots.title: WHY CAN YOU SLIDE ON ICE?
shots.purpose: Put the phenomenon on screen first: a bare frozen surface that a blade glides across with nothing added
shots.claim: ice is the only common solid that turns slippery all by itself
shots.evidence: full-bleed ink-wash macro of angular ice planes with a faint glinting sheen crossing the facets
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in across the facets: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the textbook pressure answer

subject_contract.expected_subject: full-frame macro of angular ice planes in vintage ink-wash on parchment, thin ink facet edges, faint pale sheen streaks on the surfaces, one warm rust glow near a facet edge
required: angular ice planes filling the frame
faint glinting sheen on the surfaces

one_second.relationship: a bare solid that already lets you glide

shots.purpose: State the textbook answer before breaking it: weight bearing down on ice, melt supposedly squeezed out at the contact
shots.claim: the textbook blames pressure melting, but a skate lowers the melting point by only about 0.1 degrees
shots.evidence: macro plate of one blade pressing an ice slab edge-on, a heavy rust pressure wedge into the contact and tiny droplets at the contact line
shots.motion_reason: near-static drift so the squeeze relationship is the motion
shots.transition_reason: hard cut into the lattice dive

subject_contract.expected_subject: vintage ink-wash card of a single skate blade pressing an ice slab seen edge-on, a heavy rust pressure wedge bearing down into the contact, tiny melt droplets beaded along the contact line, warm glow at the contact
required: one blade pressing an ice slab
downward rust pressure wedge at the contact
melt droplets along the contact line

one_second.relationship: weight presses down and supposedly squeezes out meltwater

shots.purpose: The signature dive: from the frozen surface down into the ordered geometry that locks the solid together
shots.claim: inside the ice, every water molecule grips four neighbours in open hexagonal rings
shots.evidence: plate of a molecular crystal lattice head-on, hexagonal node-and-bond rings shrinking toward a glowing center
shots.motion_reason: continuous zoom through the lattice: the dive IS the mechanism build
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the surface film reveal

subject_contract.expected_subject: concentric nested hexagonal lattice rings of small nodes and thin bonds shrinking toward a small glowing warm center, vintage ink-wash parchment style

one_second.relationship: each hexagonal ring is a rung deeper into the solid

shots.purpose: The contradiction and the real answer in one image: surface molecules lose half their bonds and a liquid film exists with no pressure at all
shots.claim: at the surface, molecules lose half their bonds and form a liquid film about 10 nanometers thick before any weight arrives
shots.evidence: full-bleed plate of an ordered lattice below with its topmost rings breaking open into a thin glowing liquid film
shots.motion_reason: slow rise toward the film so the breaking-bond boundary is the subject
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the glide dynamics

subject_contract.expected_subject: vintage ink-wash card of ordered hexagonal lattice rings filling the lower frame, the topmost ring row breaking open into loose small molecules and a thin horizontal glowing liquid film band with warm rust glow
required: loose molecules escaping the topmost ring row
thin glowing film band with warm glow

one_second.relationship: the solid carries its own liquid skin, pressure or no pressure

shots.purpose: The dynamics of the slip: one blade edge riding the self-made film, friction feeding the film as it glides
shots.claim: the blade rides its own lubricant, and glide friction feeds the film faster than it can refreeze
shots.evidence: plate of a single blade edge gliding left to right along a thin bright film line with faint spray arcs trailing behind
shots.motion_reason: slow pan following the glide: the film line stays fixed while the edge crosses it
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the payoff synthesis

subject_contract.expected_subject: vintage ink-wash card of a single skate blade edge gliding along a thin bright liquid film line, faint ink spray arcs trailing behind the contact, warm rust glow under the blade, no person attached to the blade
required: one blade edge gliding along a film line
thin bright film line under the blade

one_second.relationship: the blade surfs a film that its own motion renews

shots.purpose: Payoff synthesis: the whole causal chain collapsing into one image — ordered lattice beneath, liquid skin above, glide made possible
shots.claim: ice is a solid that carries its own lubricant, renewed at every touch
shots.evidence: full-bleed quiet plate of hexagonal lattice rings under a glowing liquid skin band fading into warm parchment field
shots.motion_reason: slow pull-back to the quiet wide shot; the question resolves in one image

subject_contract.expected_subject: vintage ink-wash synthesis card: nested hexagonal lattice rings in the lower half, a thin glowing liquid film band across the middle, quiet warm parchment field above with soft vignette
required: hexagonal lattice rings in the lower half
thin glowing film band across the middle

one_second.relationship: the solid and its liquid skin in one breath
